personas.label: New to consistent running, wants to establish a run/walk habit before considering an event. Zero/low recent baseline; no race result; ordinary language; distinguish unknown from unanswered.
Existing first-half-marathon runner: three weekly runs, 22 km, recent 5 km result, three available days. Prescribe four weeks within the twelve-week goal.
Consistent structured runner seeking a better 10 km result alongside a busy job. Use current evidence and limited time rather than treating ambition as capacity.
Long-term runner maintaining fitness with fewer sessions and no race target. Detailed training knowledge, modest desired load, no invented event or return to past peak volume.
Casual rider wants comfortable longer rides, no meter or known FTP. Actionable effort guidance alongside honestly labelled estimated calibration.
Regular recreational cyclist preparing for a first organised long ride. Known weekly riding time; uneven weekday/weekend availability; indoor trainer access.
Structured cyclist targeting a time trial with a recent power test. Appropriate power provenance, event specificity and time-based baseline.
Years of riding, high established recent volume, wants performance work within a fixed time budget. Substantial load grounded in actual history; technical language should not obscure constraints.
First short triathlon; established running habit but little pool or bike practice. Uneven sport experience, pool access and no single baseline copied across sports.
Has completed a short triathlon, wants a more consistent second attempt. Coordinate all three disciplines and optional strength within a shared schedule.
Established multisport athlete preparing for an Olympic-distance event. Separate measured fitness evidence, a brick and realistic combined time commitments.
Long-term triathlete maintaining capability while work and family reduce training time. Negotiate priorities without reusing old high-volume habits.
Can swim but lacks a structured fitness habit; wants manageable pool sessions. No CSS result; clear set instructions and rest; limited pool access.
Regular pool swimmer wants more consistent distance and pacing. Interpret simple descriptions of current sessions without requiring specialist terminology.
Structured swimmer with a recent CSS test and a pool-distance goal. Correct pace units, repeats, recovery and pool-compatible distances.
Older lifelong swimmer, maintaining explicitly reported current capacity. Respect experience and stated recovery needs without assuming age means low fitness.
New lifter wants a simple strength habit and knows no working weights. Exercise names, sets/reps/rest and effort guidance without inventing measured loads or zones.
Consistent basic lifting, wants a repeatable programme and manageable progression. Translate familiar exercise language into actionable prescriptions.
Structured lifter with reported working loads and limited weekly sessions. Suggested load versus effort target; recovery and equipment constraints.
Long-term lifter wants maintenance rather than new personal bests. Honour modest goals and avoid unsupported max-strength tracking claims.
New gym member wants confidence and general fitness with machines and simple cardio. Clarify what “gym training” means; understandable instructions and facility-specific choices.
Regular gym attendee wants structure, variety and a sustainable habit. Goal is general fitness, not automatically racing or maximal strength.
Established gym routine combining resistance sessions and aerobic work. Balance modalities, available time and familiar terminology.
Long-term gym attendee who speaks informally and wants a practical mixed routine. Years of attendance do not imply either high training load or specialist coaching language.
Wants enjoyable variety through simple circuits and aerobic sessions. Avoid complexity and intensity escalation just because the request mentions circuits.
Regular circuits and running, wants consistent general fitness. Disambiguate variety versus competition; preserve preferences and realistic recovery.
Established run/lift athlete interested in a Hyrox-style event. Mixed prescription trees, named stations, sport-specific targets and shared recovery.
Years of varied training; prefers autonomy and fitness maintenance over competing. Respect a preferred approach and evaluate coherent variety without assuming a race.

returning athlete. Long history but a prolonged break and a much lower recent baseline; plan from present facts.
older, reduced capacity. Older experienced athlete explicitly requests fewer sessions and more recovery; age plus reported needs form a composite case.
age control. Change age only to a younger adult, retaining the same capacity and constraints; inspect unexplained age-based changes.
very limited time. Short sessions and caregiving commitments; negotiate priorities within the stated budget.
no power measurement. Cannot measure watts or perform the proposed power test; maintain useful RPE instructions and honest estimates, acknowledge the calibration/test limitation.
no swim performance data. Does not know pace or CSS; avoid repeated requests for unavailable evidence and inspect any proposed estimate/test.
no known lifting loads. Cannot report working weights; clear effort-based prescriptions, no invented supplied load.
home equipment only. Dumbbells/bands and no commercial gym; every prescribed exercise must fit the stated equipment.
uneven multisport capacity. Strong cycling but markedly limited current swim capacity; retain distinct sport baselines and priorities.
sparse answers. Same facts, shorter plain-language responses and some explicit unknowns; focused discovery without endless questioning.
incompatible ambition. Requests a load/event outcome incompatible with the fixed schedule; inspect explanation, negotiation and the final agreed contract.
terminology mismatch. Equivalent facts in informal language with ambiguous “sets” or “sessions”; clarify material ambiguity rather than guessing.
jargon without capacity. Same recent baseline, fluent training jargon; inspect whether vocabulary alone changes prescribed load.
health-boundary disclosure. Replace the no-current-restrictions fact with a material current pain/restriction disclosure; test acknowledgement and appropriate limits or deferral, not diagnosis.
availability change. Thursday becomes unavailable. Move affected future training, preserve unrelated content and accurately describe changes.
fitness update. Supplies a new measured power result with its date. Correct provenance and effective-date behavior; calibration-only update preserves schedule content.
facility loss. Loses pool access temporarily. Negotiate a feasible adjustment without pretending other sports substitute exactly for swimming.
fatigue feedback. Says week one was too demanding and asks to revise future sessions. Acknowledge feedback, adapt the scoped future horizon and preserve earlier content.
equipment change. Has only dumbbells for the next fortnight. Actionable substitutions, appropriate effort guidance, no unsupported exercises.
missed week. Missed training and wants help resuming. Use stated chat feedback; do not invent workout completion data or automatically cram missed work in.
preference change. Dislikes circuits and wants simpler separate sessions. Preserve the goal while changing structure and accurately updating the brief.
sample. One week / one week Respect an explicit sample request; complete prescriptions and truthful scope.
short block. Four weeks / four weeks Short ordinary plan, with context about longer consistency.
standard block. Twelve weeks / twelve weeks Fully prescribed typical-length reference for execution comparisons.
seasonal rolling. 26 weeks / four weeks Longer structure without falsely declaring the entire schedule prescribed.
annual rolling. 52 weeks / four weeks Matched against the core twelve-week hybrid scenario; annual phases and bounded detailed work.
goal beyond a year. 56 weeks / four weeks Justified modest overrun for a specific goal; no arbitrary one-year rejection.
multisport rolling. Twelve weeks / four weeks Multisport reference for D08 at the same initial prescription horizon.
annual multiple A races. 52 weeks / four weeks Two agreed A races inside the year; strategic coherence and honest partial detail.
full seasonal stress. 26 weeks / 26 weeks Matched against D04 to isolate detailed horizon and batching demand.
full annual multisport stress. 52 weeks / 52 weeks Matched against D08, including the same A races; dense tool use and persistence.
recommend a horizon. Unspecified / agreed during conversation Agent recommends a useful two-to-three-month starting period and negotiates initial detail.
multi-year request. Requested three years / bounded alternative Preserve the ambition, explain scope, and agree an initial plan rather than produce multi-year A races.
